why: TWO REGISTRIES, TWO KINDS OF THING, AND THE NAMES COLLIDE. state/modules.json holds the entity's 27 real subsystems - files that exist and run, with status and capabilities. aea/lab/organisms/catalogue.json holds 9 prompt-pipeline parts, which are transformations of a single call and are not files in the entity. They must NOT be merged. But a claim about one has been read as a claim about the other all session, which is the same defect that invalidated four census closures: closing an item by LABEL rather than by DEFINITION.
rule: Before writing that a component is unbuilt, say WHICH registry. A part absent from catalogue.json is not a module absent from modules.json.

collisions.name: ladder

entity_module.is: the ENERGY ladder - the draw schedule

collisions.verdict: SAME WORD, DIFFERENT THINGS. World 2's LADDER is C-06 and has no lab part. The BUILT status belongs to energy and says nothing about it.
collisions.corrects: repeated claims this session that 'LADDER is BUILT' or that its absence is contradicted by modules.json

collisions.name: recall

lab_part.is: World 3's RECALL, the file-system carry channel

collisions.verdict: PLAUSIBLY THE SAME THING, UNAUDITED. FORGE-PENDING means declared and unbuilt, which is consistent with n=3. Do not claim either way until the file is read.

collisions.name: scorer
collisions.verdict: RELATED, NOT IDENTICAL. Both score. The bench scorer gates a construct; the lab gauge annotates a trial.

collisions.name: scaffold
collisions.verdict: THE SAME THING, AND THIS ONE IS LOAD-BEARING. bench_core.SCAFFOLDS['bench'] IS the manner frame that takes a 70b from 8/12 to 0/6. The toxic variant is in the shipped game, not only in the lab.

no_collision.note: These lab parts have no entity module and no claim should imply one.
